title: water-energy-coopt: household water and electricity co-optimisation - Sustainable Cities and Society 2021 paper model
description:
The mixed-integer programs behind Jones (2021), Sustainable Cities and Society 64, 102515, on co-optimising distributed water and electricity technologies across community scales.

Two models at two scales. The base household model is ported from its GAMS original to Python and reproduces the published optimum exactly - 30336.4771, against a GAMS/CPLEX run solved with both the relative and absolute gaps at zero, so the target is a proven optimum rather than an incumbent inside a band. At 233 rows by 214 columns it fits the free solver bundled with pip install gurobipy, verified by solving under that licence rather than by counting variables. The full co-optimisation model behind the paper's figures is 799,394 by 900,467, needs a commercial solver, and is preserved as GAMS source rather than reimplemented.

Two notebooks. One verifies the published result with no solver and no licence at all; the other builds the whole base model by hand and asserts it agrees with the packaged implementation. Both ship executed.

What a reader cannot reproduce, stated plainly: the published figures. Their inputs derive from Pecan Street household data and are not distributed - a synthetic instance ships in their place, sampled from fitted aggregate parameters, reproducing the real optimum to within 0.384%. The 31 aggregate tables behind the paper's figures are committed, so the published numbers remain checkable without R, GAMS, or the restricted inputs.

The GAMS originals and the R that drew the published figures are archived verbatim and frozen against a committed hash manifest, with a test that fails if any of them changes.

Licensing: code is MIT; the data, tables and figures are CC BY 4.0, stated by path in LICENSE-DATA. Nothing here grants any right to the Pecan Street data, which is not included.
